what: Perplexity with the KV cache stored as f32, int8 or int4 (groups of 32 values, one f32 scale per group), token by token through the cache
command: cargo run --release --example kv_precision_ppl -- --model-path models/pythia-14m --tokens wikitext2_test.pythia-14m.u32 --window W --max-windows N
reading: Unlike SmolLM-135M (int8 within noise), Pythia-14M loses a lot with a quantized cache: int8 raises perplexity by 28 percent at 4x256 tokens (190.8 to 245.2) and 34 percent at one 2,048-token window (75.5 to 101.5); int4 collapses (5,805 and 10,350). The cause was not isolated. A group of 8 instead of 32 did not fix it (see experiment_not_committed), so coarse scales are not the whole story; tiny synthetic GPT-NeoX and LLaMA models show no cache problem in model-level tests (int8 within 0.05 nats per position), so the loss looks specific to this model's real weights; not proven. A later run that quantized only the keys or only the values showed that the keys cause all of the loss (only keys: int8 236.1, int4 7,349; only values: int8 190.9, int4 190.7). With separate key and value precision (`--key-precision f32 --value-precision int4`) the loss disappears: perplexity 190.66 against 190.83 at f32, with a cache 1.7 times smaller (905,760 against 1,566,720 bytes); int8 keys with int4 values still lose (237.0).
known_gaps: one corpus, one model per file; the SmolLM-135M report is separate
cause narrowed to the keys; why (outlier channels in the keys is a guess) and whether a per-channel key scale fixes it were not tested; group 8 did not fix it

experiment_not_committed.what: same measurement (4 windows of 256 tokens) with the quantization group set to 8 values instead of 32 in a local, reverted build
experiment_not_committed.reading: a four times finer group changed int8 from 245.2 to 234.3 and int4 from 5,805 to 4,983, so the group size does not explain the loss

experiment_keys_versus_values_not_commit.what: 4 windows of 256 tokens, local reverted build where one of keys or values stayed f32 and the other used the chosen precision (group of 32)
experiment_keys_versus_values_not_commit.reading: All of the loss comes from quantizing the keys. Quantizing only the values is free on this model, even at int4.
